Cambridge Schizoanalytica is a contemporary
research collective and conceptual apparatus
dedicated to developing post-psychoanalytic
clinical theory. It represents a fusion of clinical
phenomenology, critical theory, and "operative
philology," heavily drawing upon the philosophical
concept of schizoanalysis originally formulated by
Gilles Deleuze and Félix Guattari. @ Zenodo +4
The project operates primarily through dense,
multi-author theoretical publications and digital
archive drops. @ Zenodo +1
Core Concepts and Philosophy
Cambridge Schizoanalytica positions its work as an
intervention into how meaning, speech, and human
psychology interact with modern technology
—specifically targeting the era of large
language models (LLMs) and automated
terminology. @ Academia.edu +1
e The Heteronym Structure: The primary
theoretical output of the group is credited to
Dr. Orin Trace, a persona established as a
heteronym (a constructed authorial alter-ego)
created by researcher and writer Lee Sharks.
@® Zenodo
e Operative Philology: Moving beyond standard
